title: Shared hooks must distinguish inactive installs from failures
body: A shared hook configuration does not establish that each developer has installed Mason or initialized the checkout. In an isolated 0.16.1 reproduction, missing Mason exited 127; an installed command without local setup repeatedly warned. A PATH-only guard addresses only the first case. The 0.16.2 implementation makes both inactive cases quiet while preserving visible corrupt-setup and active-check failures. Status still distinguishes configuration from observed activation, and MCP remains strict. Regression tests cover these boundaries. Preserve pre-edit coverage for shell and unknown tools when reducing overhead: editor-only or post-only matching loses original evidence. Read-only observations must not advance audit freshness or imply a new passing check. This record captures the rationale and tested implementation, not an independently accepted constraint or a guarantee about every host configuration.

content.title: Shared hooks must distinguish inactive installs from failures
content.body: A shared hook configuration does not establish that each developer has installed Mason or initialized the current checkout. In an isolated 0.16.1 reproduction on 2026-09-09, the generated command with Mason absent from PATH exited 127; with Mason installed but no local setup receipt it exited 0 while emitting a setup warning on every invocation. A PATH-only guard addresses only the first case. Proposed behavior: inactive integrations should avoid repeated warnings, while an active integration must still report failed evidence capture and unknown verification. Setup, status, and teardown should own this behavior consistently. Preserve pre-edit coverage for shell and unknown tools when reducing hook overhead; editor-only or post-only matching loses that coverage. This proposal records reproduced behavior and recommended constraints, not an implemented fix or approved design.
